newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FAA weighs more cargo safety restrictions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FAA weighs more cargo safety restrictions.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration is considering more safety restrictions for cargo shipments, the Acting Administrator told Reuters.
"We are continuing to look at cargo," acting FAA Administrator Barry Valentine said. He said the FAA is looking at both hazardous materials shipments and general cargo.
"We want to make sure nothing dangerous is on an aircraft and that everything that is there is what is supposed to be there," he said.

Hazardous materials, specifically improperly handled oxygen generators, were suspected as the cause of the crash of a ValuJet Inc aircraft in the Florida Everglades last year. After the crash of Trans World Airlines Inc Flight 800 off Long Island, New York, early concerns centered on explosives in the cargo hold.
Although Valentine said the FAA had "nothing specific" in the works, he said the agency is evaluating recommendations in the recently issued Gore Commission report on Aviation Safety.
"There are some things we can do without legislation; others will require legislation," he said.
And Valentine told a conference that a new FAA Administrator will likely be named in a matter of days.
A new administrator could shift priorities for the agency.
